conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 The Law of Chemical Equivalence
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 The Law of Chemical Equivalence

summaryBox.title: Equivalence Law
summaryBox.takeaway: Equivalents of Oxidant = Equivalents of Reductant. n_eq = n × n-factor = (w/M) × n-factor = N × V(L).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LAW OF CHEMICAL EQUIVALENCE

   Equivalents of Oxidant = Equivalents of Reductant
   n_eq = (w / M) × n-factor = N × V_(L)
   Equivalent Mass (E.M.) = Molar Mass / n-factor
   Normality (N) = Molarity (M) × n-factor
conceptBreakdown.content:
In stoichiometry, 1 Equivalent of an oxidant reacts completely with 1 Equivalent of a reductant regardless of stoichiometric coefficients:
$$\mathbf{\text{Equivalents of Oxidant} = \text{Equivalents of Reductant}}$$
$$\mathbf{n_{\text{eq}} = n \times n\text{-factor} = \frac{w}{M} \times n\text{-factor} = N \times V_{(\text{L})}}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{Equivalent Mass (E.M.)} = \frac{\text{Molar Mass } M}{n\text{-factor}}}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{Normality } N = \text{Molarity } M \times n\text{-factor}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 General n-Factor Definitions
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 General n-Factor Definitions
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
n-FACTOR DEFINITIONS MATRIX

• Acids: Basicity (number of replaceable H⁺ ions, e.g., H₂SO₄ = 2, H₃PO₃ = 2, H₃PO₂ = 1)
• Bases: Acidity (number of replaceable OH⁻ ions, e.g., Ca(OH)₂ = 2)
• Salts: Total positive or negative charge in salt matrix (e.g., Al₂(SO₄)₃ = 6)
• Redox Agents: Total change in oxidation number per mole of reactant.
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Acids**: $n = \text{Basicity}$ (number of $\text{H}^+$ released per molecule). Note: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 = 3$, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 = 2$ (one P-H bond), $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2 = 1$ (two P-H bonds).
2. **Bases**: $n = \text{Acidity}$ (number of $\text{OH}^-$ released per molecule).
3. **Salts**: $n = \text{Total positive/negative charge}$ (*e.g., $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \implies 2 \times (+3) = 6$*).
4. **Redox Agents**: $n = \text{Total change in ON per mole of reactant}$.

quickRevision: In every complete reaction: Equivalents of A = Equivalents of B.
For H₃PO₃, basicity is 2; for H₃PO₂, basicity is 1.
